description: StEER - Puerto Rico Earthquake Sequence December 2019 to January 2020: Field Assessment Structural Team (FAST) Early Access Reconnaissance Report (EARR) is a dataset listed in DesignSafe Data Depot (published projects), a research data repository for natural hazards engineering under the section "other", published or maintained by Tracy Kijewski-Correa, University of Notre Dame (nd.edu). A sequence of earthquakes occurred in the southwestern region of Puerto Rico, initiating at the end of 2019. The first widely-felt earthquake occurred on December 28th, 2019 with a Mw 5.0 magnitude. Coverage: as described in the project (site or event named in the description). DesignSafe files it as a "other" project. Its DOI is 10.17603/ds2-h0kd-5677. Keywords: StEER, Reconnaissance, EARR, earthquake, Puerto Rico, Guánica. Published 2020-03-03. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is CC-BY-4.0 (labelled "Creative Commons Attribution" on the DesignSafe project). Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support structural performance, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-designsafe-data-depot-repository.
